## Problem
Feature to add: Satisfying cash-in feedback: when ore reaches the owner's collector, the server fires a CashIn remote to that owner with the amount, the ore tier and the collector position. A client CashInFx script then plays a short coin 'cha-ching' sound (pitch rises slightly with tier; use sound ids that load in Studio, e.g. rbxasset://sounds/electronicpingshort.wav), bursts a ParticleEmitter of gold sparkles at the collector, floats a '+$N' BillboardGui text that rises and fades (colored by tier), and pulses the HUD cash label. Purchases play an upgrade 'pop' sound with a confetti burst; throttle effects so at most 6 popups per second. The collector itself gets a glowing PointLight and a slowly spinning neon ring. Bump counter cashin_fx_sent.
Change needed in this file: At the existing point where a cube or ore reaches the owner's collector and the owner's Cash is credited, require CashInService and call CashInService.cashIn(ownerPlayer, amountCredited, oreTier, collectorPart.Position), using the amount and tier the existing code already computes. Do not change the cash math, and do not add any telemetry call here.
New feature files: ReplicatedStorage/CashInConfig.luau, ServerScriptService/CashInService.luau, StarterPlayerScripts/CashInFx.client.luau. Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: cashin_fx_sent, purchase_fx_sent.

## Context
Watch cubes roll down your conveyor, cash in, and buy droppers and speed upgrades to grow your tiny factory!

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.

## Luau and Roblox APIs
- The base place is empty: build the map from code (Instance.new Parts, Anchored = true, parented to Workspace).
- Get services with game:GetService("Players") etc.; use task.wait / task.spawn / task.delay, never wait / spawn / delay.
- Players.PlayerAdded can fire before your script connects in a playtest: also loop over Players:GetPlayers() once at startup.
- Wait for characters with player.CharacterAdded (and player.Character if already present); use WaitForChild with a timeout across the client/server boundary.
- ModuleScripts must return exactly one value (usually a table); require them by path, e.g. require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Config")).
- Create RemoteEvents on the server in one place; clients only WaitForChild them and handle nil after the timeout.
- Bump counters for key gameplay events with require(ReplicatedStorage.ForgeTelemetry).count("name", 1) (server only) so playtests can verify the core loop. Include counters for purchases and other branches that need verification.
- Count each telemetry counter in exactly one place (the module that owns the event). Duplicate count calls push once-only counters past their expected value.
- Touched fires many times per touch: debounce per player (a per-player cooldown or a one-time purchased flag) and check and deduct cost in the same step to prevent double-buys or double-spends.
- Define the data shape that a builder module returns (field names such as origin, gate, spawn) once, and have consumers use those exact fields. Do not add `a or b` fallbacks for guessed names.

## UI kit (house style for all UI: paste the snippets you use, Theme first, and adapt; plain Luau, not modules)
- Chunky text: every label gets a dark UIStroke (2.5-4 px). LuckiestGuy for titles/numbers, FredokaOne for body. Never default or thin fonts.
- One palette everywhere: yellow Primary = main action, green Good = affordable/claim, red Bad = close/can't, blue Info = secondary, dark Ink outlines.
- Depth: UICorner 12-18 px, UIStroke border, light-top UIGradient fill, hard drop shadow 4-6 px below.
- Everything moves: appear with a Back-eased UIScale pop (0 -> 1), react with a punch (1.2 -> 1), press squish to 0.9. Tween UIScale, not Size; 0.1-0.4 s, never linear.
- Numbers tick up and pop on change, big values short ("12.5K"); gains flash green, losses red.
- Every action gives feedback: toast, floating "+N" or reward popup. Max 3 toasts.
- Mobile first: 1280x720 offsets under a viewport UIScale (`Theme.screen`), safe insets, buttons >= 44 px, nothing key in the top-left (Roblox menu).
- HUD hugs the edges, centre stays clear; windows open over a dim backdrop with a close X.
- World prices on BillboardGuis: green when affordable, red when not.
- UI is built in code with Instance.new, no image asset ids (emoji/letters for icons), ResetOnSpawn = false.

### PriceBillboard.luau (World price tag on a buy pad / shop item (BillboardGui), green when affordable. Works in server Scripts.)
```luau
-- PriceBillboard: world price tag over a buy pad / shop item; green when affordable, red when not. Server or client.
-- Standalone (no Theme needed) so a server Script can paste it too.
local function priceBillboard(part: BasePart, title: string, price: number): (BillboardGui, (boolean) -> ())
	local bb = Instance.new("BillboardGui")
	bb.Size, bb.StudsOffset = UDim2.fromScale(6, 2.2), Vector3.new(0, part.Size.Y / 2 + 2, 0)
	bb.AlwaysOnTop, bb.MaxDistance, bb.LightInfluence = false, 80, 0
	bb.Adornee = part
	local function text(t: string, y: number, h: number, color: Color3): TextLabel
		local l = Instance.new("TextLabel")
		l.Size, l.Position, l.BackgroundTransparency = UDim2.fromScale(1, h), UDim2.fromScale(0, y), 1
		l.Text, l.Font, l.TextScaled, l.TextColor3 = t, Enum.Font.LuckiestGuy, true, color
		local s = Instance.new("UIStroke")
		s.Thickness, s.Color = 3, Color3.fromRGB(28, 22, 38)
		s.Parent = l
		l.Parent = bb
		return l
	end
	text(title, 0, 0.45, Color3.fromRGB(255, 248, 232))
	local cost = text("$" .. tostring(price), 0.45, 0.55, Color3.fromRGB(240, 68, 64))
	bb.Parent = part
	local function setAffordable(ok: boolean)
		cost.TextColor3 = if ok then Color3.fromRGB(88, 214, 92) else Color3.fromRGB(240, 68, 64)
	end
	return bb, setAffordable -- client: call setAffordable(cash.Value >= price) on cash.Changed
end
```
